answers.how: The small bird is about 47 px long, giving 0.94/47 = 0.020 m/px. The big bird is about 76 px long.
The big bird's maximum visible wingtip-to-wingtip width is about 149 px. Multiplying by 0.020 m/px gives 2.98 m.
The small bird's maximum visible wingtip-to-wingtip width is about 87 px. Multiplying by 0.020 m/px gives 1.74 m.
Between frames 2 and 8, the small bird moves about 245 px in 0.250 s. Using 0.020 m/px gives 19.6 m/s.
Between frames 2 and 4, the big bird moves about 134 px in 2/24 s. Using 0.020 m/px gives approximately 32.2 m/s.
Extrapolating the observed horizontal motion to 0.5 s gives a center-to-center separation of about 1,400 px. At 0.020 m/px, this is 28.0 m.
